scope: Current official entry points and practical usage boundaries for Bay Area transportation and parking platforms.
method: Official provider, transportation-agency or government pages only. Direct page text and official search-indexed extracts are labeled separately. Best-for and sequencing advice is editorial guidance. No account login, purchase, ride request, fare quote, parking reservation or interactive live-coverage test was performed.

formatMeaning.app-web: An official app and at least one useful browser service are documented; this does not promise feature parity or browser-based ride unlocking.
formatMeaning.app: The entry recommends the rider app. Its URL is the official information/download entry, not a third-party store mirror.
formatMeaning.web: The recommended current tool is the official website; no standalone active app is implied.

sources.title: Google Maps
facts: Official Maps product entry point, with access to mapping, navigation and saved places.
sources.limits: Official Google product page used as the public entry and download-information source; no third-party download URL is used.

sources.title: Google Maps Help — Get directions
facts: Supports multiple travel modes and directions based on departure or arrival date and time.
sources.limits: Official indexed directions help supports travel modes and departure/arrival planning. No sample route or live arrival estimate was independently tested.

sources.title: Google Maps Help — Offline maps
facts: Offline mode does not provide transit, walking or cycling directions, or live traffic.
sources.limits: Official indexed offline-map instructions identify the unavailable offline modes. Offline driving guidance is not represented as offline public-transit navigation.

sources.title: 511 Open Data
facts: Bay Area transportation data is supplied to mapping and travel applications, including Google, Apple and Transit.
Regional transportation data is supplied to partner applications including Apple.
sources.limits: Official indexed content lists Google, Apple and Transit as users or partners for regional transportation data. This does not establish complete live predictions for every operator.

sources.title: Apple Maps
facts: The official entry point describes detailed San Francisco maps, directions and live transit information where available.
sources.limits: Official Apple product page confirms San Francisco detailed maps and transit functionality where available. The article does not claim an Android native app or native/web feature parity.

sources.title: Apple Support — Maps on the web
facts: Maps on the web supports multiple desktop and mobile browsers; features can vary by platform.
sources.limits: The support article was opened directly. Its supported-browser guidance establishes current web availability; interactive Maps rendering was not tested.

sources.title: Transit — SF Bay Area
facts: Lists supported Bay Area operators and provides app downloads, trip planning, arrivals and service alerts.
sources.limits: Read the Bay Area operator list directly, including Muni, BART, Caltrain, AC Transit, VTA, SMART and ferry. The official Plan a trip link resolves to a JavaScript interface; no route was submitted.

sources.title: Transit Help — Royale FAQ
facts: Some extended features are provided through Royale, which may be sponsored by a transit agency.
sources.limits: Official indexed help content supports the Royale limitation. Subscription prices and agency sponsorship were not generalized to all Bay Area riders.

sources.title: Clipper — Clipper on Your Phone
facts: Explains app-based account management, mobile wallets, card transfers and deactivation of the plastic card for transit.
sources.limits: Direct text distinguishes registering a plastic card from adding a card to a mobile wallet, and says plastic cards transferred to a wallet are deactivated for transit. It does not support universal transit, bike-share or parking acceptance.

sources.title: SFMTA — MuniMobile
facts: Single-ride ticket sales ended September 1, 2026. Some other fare products remain on sale in 2026; the full transition is not yet complete.
sources.limits: Direct current page says single-ride sales ended September 1, 2026. Other listed passes remain during 2026; a full transition planned for mid-2027 is not treated as already complete. No standalone current general-purpose ticketing recommendation was created.

sources.title: BART — Official App
facts: The official app provides trip planning, live arrivals, service and elevator alerts, and parking features.
sources.limits: Direct app page provides official store links and planning, arrival, elevator and parking features. A legacy Google Pay rollout sentence on this page was not used; current wallet facts come from Clipper.

sources.title: BART — Parking Payment
facts: Explains parking products and payment; parking cannot be paid from Clipper balance.
sources.limits: Official indexed text explains parking payment and that Clipper balance cannot pay parking. No fixed daily or reserved parking price is reproduced.

sources.title: Caltrain — How to Ride
facts: Explains schedule lookup, stopping patterns, South County connections and the requirement to pay before boarding.
sources.limits: Official indexed rider instructions support route patterns, weekday South County service and payment before boarding. No fixed departures or assumption of full weekend Gilroy service is made.

sources.title: Caltrain — Mobile App Retirement FAQ
facts: The old ticketing app retired on October 31, 2025; riders should use current options such as Clipper or ticket machines.
sources.limits: The official indexed FAQ contains the October 31, 2025 retirement date. A direct open returned timetable content rather than the FAQ body; the retirement fact is therefore labeled indexed evidence, not a successful direct FAQ read. A planned ParkMobile rollout mentioned in that old FAQ was not treated as completed.

sources.title: 511 — Bay Area Transportation
facts: Provides live traffic, transit and cycling alerts, a regional map, operator resources and telephone information.
The regional website lists Bay Wheels service in San Francisco, the East Bay and San Jose, with a map lookup.
sources.limits: Direct homepage supports real-time regional alerts, map resources, phone 511, and Bay Wheels service in San Francisco, the East Bay and San Jose. Its event promotion dates were not reused for this evergreen platform entry.

sources.title: 511 — Frequently Asked Questions
facts: Explains the regional information service and links to other applications for trip planning.
sources.limits: Official indexed FAQ used for the distinction between regional information and third-party trip-planning tools.

sources.title: Uber — San Francisco
facts: Official San Francisco ride entry point, with trip and available vehicle-option lookup.
sources.limits: Direct official city page confirms an entry point for San Francisco rides. Live driver availability, wait times and prices were not tested.

sources.title: Uber — Oakland
facts: Confirms an official ride-service entry point for Oakland.
sources.limits: Direct official city page confirms an Oakland service entry; address-by-address availability remains dynamic.

sources.title: Uber — San Jose
facts: Confirms an official ride-service entry point for San Jose.
sources.limits: Direct official city page confirms a San Jose service entry; address-by-address availability remains dynamic.

sources.title: Uber — SFO Pickup
facts: Airport pickup locations should be confirmed in the app; ride acceptance and final charges are subject to conditions.
Quotes account for demand, trip time and distance, tolls and city fees; route changes can alter the final price. The page links to Uber's browser booking service.
sources.limits: Direct current page supports app-specific pickup directions, browser ride-request links, demand/time/distance/toll/city-fee pricing factors and no guarantee of driver acceptance. Promotional percentages, average prices and inconsistent capacity examples were not reused.

sources.title: Lyft — San Francisco
facts: Describes San Francisco ride service, the app entry point, and how demand and surcharges affect prices.
sources.limits: Direct city page confirms the app-based service and that busy periods, tolls and surcharges affect prices. Classified app rather than implying an unverified ordinary consumer web-booking flow.

sources.title: Lyft — Cities
facts: The official service-city directory includes San Francisco, Oakland and San Jose.
sources.limits: Official indexed city directory lists San Francisco, Oakland and San Jose. It is not a guarantee of pickup at every address in those cities or surrounding counties.

sources.title: Lyft — Airports
facts: The official airport directory includes SFO, OAK and SJC; pickups must follow the airport's designated arrangements.
sources.limits: Official indexed airport directory lists SFO, OAK and SJC. Current pickup instructions are left to each booking; no fixed terminal curb is prescribed.

sources.title: Waymo — Rides
facts: Official ride and app entry point; rides are requested in the app.
sources.limits: Direct official rider page used for the app entry. No booking, quoted fare or per-address availability was tested.

sources.title: Waymo Help — Service Areas
facts: The official service-area page lists the San Francisco Bay Area; use the service map and app to confirm boundaries.
sources.limits: The page directly lists the San Francisco Bay Area with a service-map image. The image boundary was not independently digitized or audited; the entry explicitly requires both endpoints to be checked in the app.

sources.title: Waymo Help — Bay Area Expansion
facts: A May 2026 announcement adds more service locations in San Jose and Campbell.
sources.limits: Direct official May 2026 expansion notice supports additional San Jose and Campbell destinations. It is not interpreted as full county, airport or entire Bay Area coverage.

sources.title: ParkMobile
facts: Official parking-payment and app entry point, using the location, vehicle and duration.
sources.limits: Official indexed product content supports zone/location, plate, duration and app/web parking payment. No single provider is assumed accepted at all Bay Area facilities.

sources.title: SFMTA — Mobile Parking Payment Update
facts: San Francisco meters use ParkMobile and HotSpot, with app, browser and guest-payment options.
sources.limits: Direct May 11, 2026 SFMTA announcement supports ParkMobile and HotSpot, guest/browser payment, location codes and time-limit-dependent extension. The rollout announcement alone is not used to prove the later completed PayByPhone withdrawal.

sources.title: SFMTA — Use Your Phone to Pay for Parking
facts: Current guidance confirms that SFMTA meters no longer accept PayByPhone; drivers must still verify the location code and posted time limits.
sources.limits: Direct extraction returned navigation-only content; official search-indexed page body explicitly says PayByPhone has been phased out and is no longer accepted at SFMTA meters. This is recorded as indexed body evidence, not a direct full-body read.

sources.title: HotSpot Parking
facts: Official instructions support app or browser payment, with an account or as a guest, and link to the US payment portal.
sources.limits: Direct operator page supports app or browser, account or guest and a US payment link. Generic provider QR-code functionality is not presented as an SFMTA-meter payment method.

sources.title: PayByPhone
facts: The official entry point provides app downloads and web parking payment.
sources.limits: Direct operator homepage provides official app and web-payment links. General global marketing coverage is not used to infer Bay Area acceptance.

sources.title: Presidio — Parking
facts: Presidio parking can be paid through PayByPhone or on-site pay stations; rates vary by location and date.
sources.limits: Direct Presidio page lists PayByPhone and on-site pay stations, plate entry and rates varying by location/day. The Presidio exception is kept separate from SFMTA street meters.

sources.title: SpotHero — San Francisco Parking
facts: Provides time-based search and reservation access for participating San Francisco parking facilities.
sources.limits: Official indexed city page supports local parking inventory and reservation search only. Potentially stale municipal meter hours, holidays or general parking FAQs on that marketing page were not used.

sources.title: SpotHero — FAQ
facts: Explains Parking Pass entry, vehicle restrictions, re-entry and booking-cancellation conditions.
sources.limits: Direct FAQ supports Parking Pass instructions, vehicle restrictions, no re-entry at most facilities and booking-specific cancellation/extra-charge conditions. No reservation or inventory test was performed.

sources.title: Bay Wheels — Ride Experience
facts: Official riding instructions provide app access, unlocking and green-light dock confirmation, plus online membership selection.
sources.limits: Direct official riding page supports app links, bike unlocking, online memberships and green-light dock confirmation. Its broad generic rack-parking wording was narrowed by the newer dedicated parking article.

sources.title: Lyft Bike — E-bike Parking Upgrade
facts: Some San Francisco e-bikes with locks may use public racks under the specified rules; the other listed cities still require docking.
sources.limits: Official indexed article and direct page text support the San Francisco lock-equipped e-bike rack-parking policy and docking in the other listed cities. The rule is not generalized to San Jose or every Bay Area bicycle.

sources.title: FasTrak
facts: Official entry point for toll accounts, payment and toll locations.
sources.limits: Official indexed homepage provides account, payment and toll-location entry points. No toll amount, toll discount or third-party collection link was reproduced.

sources.title: FasTrak — Ways to Pay
facts: Distinguishes payment options and tag requirements for bridges and express lanes.
sources.limits: Direct payment-options page distinguishes bridge and express-lane payment eligibility. Plate-based bridge payment is not described as sufficient for express lanes.

sources.title: FasTrak — Rental Vehicles Guide
facts: Rental cars have several toll-payment options. An existing account requires plate start and end dates; Short-Term License Plate Accounts are for bridges only.
sources.limits: Direct rental guide confirms own-account plate start/end dates and tag mounting, rental-company fees, and that Short-Term License Plate Accounts cannot pay express-lane tolls. No specific rental company's plan is endorsed.

accessLimitations.result: Direct browser-tool opening was restricted; no interactive map was read. Web availability is supported instead by Apple's directly opened browser-support article.
Followed the official SF Bay Area page's Plan a trip link. The response was a JavaScript interface with no extractable route content; no route search was performed.

Redirected to https://lyftbikes.com/; a subsequent main-page read returned an access error. The directly readable official ride-experience page and dedicated current parking article were used instead.

Official search still exposed indexed pricing content, but the parent agent's direct link audit returned HTTP 404. Removed from the published platform sources; current directly read SFO pickup/pricing guidance supports the retained pricing statement.

selectionNotes: MuniMobile is not listed as a standalone general-purpose recommendation. Single-ride sales ended September 1, 2026, while some other passes remain during 2026. The staged transition is summarized in the Clipper entry.
Caltrain is a web entry because Caltrain Mobile retired October 31, 2025. An old announcement's future ParkMobile rollout was not treated as verified current Caltrain parking acceptance.
ParkMobile and HotSpot are the current SFMTA meter choices. PayByPhone remains a narrowly scoped Presidio/participating-location entry; it is not recommended for SFMTA meters.
Waymo coverage is deliberately address-dependent. Public service, future expansion, test permits and a whole county are not treated as interchangeable.
No fixed fares, discounts, guaranteed wait times, guaranteed parking stock or universal payment acceptance are claimed.
Product entry and download-information URLs for Google Maps and Apple Maps are their own official domains.
